Effort Score, call risk flags, caller-ID rewrite rules and delisting requests for Yaxxa Omni Call Control, smoother AI agent conversations, and hang up works again on the agent desk.

Customer Effort Score: every call the AI reads now gets one 0–100 score for how hard the customer had to work, with its parts, shown by agent, team and queue. Repeat contacts count towards it, and the score goes to the warehouse export with the rest of the call analysis.

Call risk rules: every outbound call is checked against premium and high-risk number ranges, the tenant's own allowed and blocked prefixes, how many calls go out per minute and hour, repeated calls to the same number from the same caller ID, and a daily carrier spend cap. Nothing is blocked yet: the reasons are flagged on the call and show in the call records and their CSV. Admins set the rules under call risk settings; the premium-range check is on by default and a platform admin can turn it off per tenant.

Caller-ID rewrite rules: a campaign can change the caller ID after the pool has chosen it, by adding a prefix, removing one, or replacing it with another active caller ID, for carriers or countries that want the number in a different form.

Delisting requests: when a number is flagged as spam with a provider, the Number Manager opens a guided task to ask that provider to clear it. The task closes itself when a later check comes back clean on every handset, and reminds you if it has waited more than 7 days.

AI agent conversations: the AI agent no longer treats a short "mm-hm" over its answer, or the echo of its own voice, as the caller taking a turn, so it stops cutting itself off and finishes what it was saying.

Untapped handoff targets: the handoff target names come from Untapped's onboarding details. Sync now adds new names as "Not set" until you choose where they go, marks names Untapped no longer sends without deleting them, and shows when it last synced and any error.

Security: logs hide call transcripts, card numbers and signed recording links; the realtime connection limits unsigned connections per address; licence check-ins need the server's own ID before download details are given; and production refuses to start with an empty integration key or a development database password.

Fixes: the agent desk's Hang up button was being refused, so calls could not be ended from it; it works again. An agent who cannot see the customer's number can still call a missed call back, without the number being shown. Ticket alerts that are held for working hours stay inside working hours. The flow designer refuses two queues with the same name. Agent assist highlights a new suggestion even when it is the first one, and the chat widget preview shows the right icon.

Imara CX edition: a new edition for Imara installations, off unless `UCEO_EDITION=imara`, so nothing changes for Yaxxa installations. It adds public sign-up and apply-for-the-beta, an applications review for staff with custom trials and extensions, trial lifecycle emails, and Imara branding.

For operators: `install.sh --edition` picks the edition at install time, and servers without IPv6 now try IPv4 first. Installs behind Cloudflare can set `UCEO_BEHIND_PROXY` (opt-in, off by default). The web image now runs Caddy through a small wrapper. Plan forms wait for the edition to load before Save is enabled. Before installing, check that the server's `INTEGRATION_SECRET_KEY` is set and not all zeros, and that `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_PLATFORM_URL` carry no development password: production now refuses to start otherwise. `uceo-update.sh` creates the server's ID if it has none."}
